extracted.intended_audience: FCC auction participants, license applicants, designated entities, and counsel advising on competitive bidding/eligibility
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative requirements governing designated-entity benefits, bidding credits, installment payments, ownership disclosure, audits, construction prior to grant, unjust-enrichment payments, and reporting of eligibility events in FCC competitive auctions and subsequent licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal land bidding credit calculation and pro rata recalculation
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining the aggregate maximum tribal land bidding credits for which applicants for such licenses might have qualified, the Commission shall assume that any applicant seeking a tribal land bidding credit on its long-form application will be eligible for the largest tribal land bidding credit possible for its bid excepting the limitation ((f)(3)(v)). After all applications seeking a tribal land bidding credit with respect to licenses covered by a reserve price have been finally resolved, the Commission will recalculate the pro rata credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To recalculate an applicant's pro rata tribal land bidding credit, the Commission will multiply the full amount of the tribal land bidding credit for which the applicant would be eligible (excepting the limitation) by a fraction consisting of: numerator = amount by which winning bids for licenses subject to the reserve price, net of discounts the Commission takes into account when reporting net bids, exceed the reserve price; denominator = aggregate amount of tribal land bidding credits for which all applicants for such licenses would have qualified (excepting the limitation). Final determination occurs only after any review or reconsideration has concluded and no opportunity remains for further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of tribal land bidding credit and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A pending request for a bidding credit for serving qualifying tribal land has no effect on a bidder's obligations to make any auction payments prior to award of the bidding credit by the Commission. Tribal land bidding credits will be calculated and awarded prior to license grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a pro rata tribal land bidding credit is granted prior to license grant, the Commission will recalculate the applicant's pro rata credit after all relevant applications are finally resolved; if a recalculated credit is larger than the previously awarded credit, the Commission will award the difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-construction certification for tribal land bidding credit recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Within fifteen (15) days of the third anniversary of the initial grant of its license, a recipient of a bidding credit must file a certification that it has constructed and is operating a system capable of serving seventy-five (75) percent of the population of the qualifying tribal land for which the credit was awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient must provide the total population of the tribal area covered by its license and the number of persons that it is serving in the tribal area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance penalties for failure to certify construction
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient of a bidding credit fails to provide the post-construction certification required, it shall repay the bidding credit amount in its entirety, plus interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest is based on the rate for ten-year U.S. Treasury obligations applicable on the date the license is granted. Payment must be made within thirty (30) days of the third anniversary of the initial grant. Failure to repay the amount and interest within required time results in automatic termination of the license without specific Commission action. Repayment does not affect calculation of amounts available for tribal land bidding credits pursuant to (f)(3)(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural service provider bidding credit eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A winning bidder that qualifies as a rural service provider and has not claimed a small business bidding credit will be eligible to receive a 15 percent bidding credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of this paragraph, a rural service provider means a service provider that: (A) is in the business of providing commercial communications services and together with its controlling interests, affiliates, and affiliates of controlling interests has fewer than 250,000 combined wireless, wireline, broadband, and cable subscribers as of the short-form filing deadline; and (B) serves predominantly rural areas, defined as counties with population density of 100 or fewer persons per square mile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size attribution for rural service provider eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The combined wireless, wireline, broadband, and cable subscribers of the applicant (or licensee), its affiliates, its controlling interests, and the affiliates of its controlling interests shall be attributed to the applicant and considered on a cumulative basis for determining eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: For rural partnerships providing service as of July 16, 2015, the Commission will determine eligibility by evaluating whether individual members of the rural partnership individually have fewer than 250,000 combined subscribers; for those partnerships subscribers will not be aggregated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap on winning bid discount for rural service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum total discount that a winning bidder eligible for a rural service provider bidding credit may receive will be established on an auction-by-auction basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The limit on the discount will be no less than $10 million; the Commission may adopt a market-based cap on an auction-by-auction basis to establish an overall limit on discount for certain license areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installment payments: eligibility and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may permit small businesses (including those owned by women, minorities, or rural telephone companies that qualify as small businesses) and other entities determined eligible on a service-specific basis, which are high bidders for specified licenses, to pay the full amount of their high bids in installments over the term of their licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is service-specific and subject to Commission specification in public notices or service rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial post-auction deposit requirement for installment payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each eligible applicant paying for its license(s) on an installment basis must deposit by wire transfer sufficient additional funds to bring its total deposits to ten (10) percent of its winning bid(s) within ten (10) days after the Commission has declared it the winning bidder and closed the bidding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to remit the required payment will make the bidder liable to pay a default payment pursuant to § 1.2104(g)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Second down payment to commence installment plan and late payment allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Within ten (10) days of the conditional grant of the license application, the licensee shall pay another ten (10) percent of the high bid, thereby commencing the eligible licensee's installment payment plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the winning bidder fails to submit this additional ten percent by the deadline it may make payment within ten (10) business days after the deadline provided it also pays a late fee equal to five percent of the amount due. Failure to submit the second down payment plus any late fee by the late payment deadline results in being considered in default and subject to applicable default payments. Licenses will be awarded upon full and timely payment of second down payments and any applicable late fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installment plan security and standard terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon grant of the license, the Commission will notify each eligible licensee of the terms of its installment payment plan and that it must execute a promissory note and security agreement as a condition of the installment payment plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless other terms are specified for particular services, such plans will: (i) impose interest based on the rate of U.S. Treasury obligations with maturities closest to the license term at time of licensing; (ii) allow installment payments for the full license term; (iii) begin with interest-only payments for first two years; and (iv) amortize principal and interest over the remaining term.

rubrics_metrics.name: License conditioned on timely performance of installment obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A license granted to an eligible entity that elects installment payments shall be conditioned upon the full and timely performance of the licensee's payment obligations under the installment plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly payment grace periods and late fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any licensee that fails to submit its quarterly installment payment may submit such payment on or before the last day of the next quarter (first additional quarter) without being considered delinquent and will be assessed a late payment fee equal to five percent of the past due Required Installment Payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If payment is not made by the end of the first additional quarter, the licensee may submit by the last day of the second additional quarter and will be assessed a ten percent late fee. No form is required to take advantage of these grace periods. Payments made at close of any grace period will first be applied to lender advances, then late fees, then interest charges, then installment payments for the most back-due quarterly installment payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default for failure to pay within two quarters
rubrics_metrics.description: If an eligible entity fails to pay the total Required Installment Payment, interest and any late fees within two quarters (6 months) of the Required Installment Payment due date, it shall be in default, its license shall automatically cancel, and it will be subject to debt collection procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A licensee in the PCS C or F blocks shall be in default and its license shall automatically cancel and be subject to debt collection if the payment due on the payment resumption date is more than 90 days delinquent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission discretion on upfront payment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may establish different upfront payment requirements for categories of designated entities in competitive bidding rules of particular auctionable services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of designated-entity preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may offer designated entities a combination of the available preferences or additional preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form disclosure of agreements affecting designated entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated entities must describe on their long-form applications how they satisfy the requirements for eligibility for designated entity status, and must list and summarize on their long-form applications all agreements that affect designated entity status such as partnership agreements, shareholder agreements, management agreements, spectrum leasing arrangements, spectrum resale (including wholesale) arrangements, spectrum use agreements, and all other agreements, including oral agreements, establishing de facto or de jure control of the entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated entities must also provide the date(s) on which they entered into each listed agreement and file a copy of each such agreement. To enable Commission audits, awarded designated entities must, for the term of the license, maintain at their facilities or with designated agents the lists, summaries, dates and copies required and those required by § 1.2114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortia qualification for designated entity provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may, on a service-specific basis, permit consortia, each member of which individually meets the eligibility requirements, to qualify for any designated entity provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly-traded minority- or women-owned companies eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may, on a service-specific basis, permit publicly-traded companies that are owned by members of minority groups or women to qualify for any designated entity provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audits of applicants and licensees claiming designated-entity eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and licensees claiming eligibility shall be subject to audits by the Commission, using in-house and contract resources. Selection for audit may be random, on information, or on other factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent to such audits is part of the short-form application (FCC Form 175) and includes consent to audit books, documents and other material (including accounting procedures and practices), inspection of facilities engaged in providing or transacting business or keeping FCC-license records, and consent to interview principals, employees, customers and suppliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reports by designated entity licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: Each designated entity licensee must file with the Commission an annual report no later than September 30 of each year for each license it holds that was acquired using designated entity benefits and that, as of August 31 of the year in which the report is due, remains subject to designated entity unjust enrichment requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annual report must provide the information described for the reporting year. If during the reporting year a designated entity assigned or transferred a designated entity license, the designated entity that holds the license on September 30 of the year in which the application for the transaction is filed is responsible for filing the annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report shall include, at a minimum, a list and summaries of all agreements and arrangements (including proposed agreements and arrangements) that relate to eligibility for designated entity benefits. This list must include the parties (including affiliates, controlling interests, and affiliates of controlling interests) to each agreement, as well as the dates on which the parties entered into each agreement or arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the information has already been filed and remains current, the designated entity may instead include the ULS file number and date of the report or application containing the current information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross revenues definition for eligibility purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross revenues shall mean all income received by an entity, whether earned or passive, before any deductions are made for costs of doing business, as evidenced by audited financial statements for the relevant most recently completed calendar years or most recently completed fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an entity was not in existence for the relevant period, gross revenues shall be evidenced by audited financial statements of a predecessor-in-interest or, if none, unaudited financial statements certified by the applicant as accurate. When audited statements are not used, gross revenues may be certified by the chief financial officer or equivalent and must be prepared in accordance with GAAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total assets definition for eligibility purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Total assets shall mean the book value (except where GAAP require market valuation) of all property owned by an entity, whether real or personal, tangible or intangible, as evidenced by the most recently audited financial statements or certified by the applicant's chief financial officer if audited statements are not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unjust enrichment payments: installment financing upon assignment/transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: If a licensee that utilizes installment financing seeks to assign or transfer control of its license to an entity not meeting the eligibility standards for installment payments, the licensee must make full payment of the remaining unpaid principal and any unpaid interest accrued through the date of assignment or transfer as a condition of approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a licensee seeks to make a change in ownership structure resulting in losing eligibility for installment payments, the licensee shall first seek Commission approval and must make full payment of remaining unpaid principal and unpaid interest accrued through the date of such change as a condition of approval. Increases in gross revenues or total assets due to nonattributable equity investments, debt financing, revenue from operations or other investment shall not be considered to result in losing eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unjust enrichment payments: bidding credits upon assignment/transfer or ownership change
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee that utilizes a bidding credit and seeks to assign or transfer control of a license to an entity that does not meet eligibility criteria for a bidding credit will be required to reimburse the U.S. Government for the amount of the bidding credit, plus interest based on the rate for ten-year U.S. Treasury obligations applicable on the date the license was granted, as a condition of approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the acquiring party is eligible for a lower bidding credit, the difference between the original and the acquiring party's credit, plus interest, must be paid. If an ownership change results in losing eligibility or qualifying for a lower bidding credit during the initial term, the amount (or difference) plus interest must be paid as a condition of approval of the assignment, transfer, or a reportable eligibility event (see § 1.2114).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment schedule reducing unjust enrichment over license term
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of payments made pursuant to unjust enrichment for bidding credits will be reduced over time as follows: transfer in first two years → forfeiture of 100% of value; transfer in year 3 → 75% forfeiture; year 4 → 50%; year 5 → 25%; year 6 or thereafter → no payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These payments must be paid to the United States Treasury as a condition of approval of the assignment, transfer, ownership change or reportable eligibility event (see § 1.2114).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unjust enrichment for partitioning and disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees making installment payments that partition licenses or disaggregate spectrum to entities not meeting eligibility standards will be subject to unjust enrichment provisions; similarly for licensees that received bidding credits and partition or disaggregate spectrum to ineligible entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unjust enrichment payments for partitioned license areas are calculated based on ratio of population of partitioned area to overall population using most recent census data. For disaggregated spectrum, payments are based on ratio of amount of spectrum disaggregated to the amount of spectrum held by the licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership disclosure requirements for short-form and other applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application to participate in competitive bidding (short-form FCC Form 175), or for a license, authorization, assignment, or transfer of control shall fully disclose: (1) real party or parties in interest including identity and relationship of those directly or indirectly owning or controlling the applicant; (2) name, address, citizenship of any party holding 10% or more of stock; (3) limited partnership limited partners with 10%+ interests; (4) general partnership partners and shares; (5) LLC members with 10%+; (6) all parties holding indirect ownership interests determined by successive multiplication equal to 10% or more (with >50% treated as 100%); and (7) any FCC-regulated entity or applicant in which the applicant or parties identified hold 10%+ including description of principal business and relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional disclosure requirements for claiming designated entity status on short-form
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to standard ownership disclosures, each applicant claiming eligibility for small business provisions or a rural service provider bidding credit shall disclose on its short-form: names, addresses, citizenship of all officers, directors, affiliates and other controlling interests; any FCC-regulated entity in which controlling interests own 10%+ including description of business and relationship; all parties with which the applicant has agreements for use of spectrum capacity; separately and in the aggregate gross revenues for the applicant, affiliates, controlling interests and affiliates; information demonstrating rural service provider criteria if claiming that credit; and if a consortium, provide the information separately for each member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit requirements to license/assignment/transfer applications
rubrics_metrics.description: As an exhibit to its application for a license, authorization, assignment, or transfer of control, an applicant must: list names/addresses/citizenship of officers, directors, and controlling interests; list any FCC-regulated entities in which controlling interests own 10%+; list and summarize all agreements or instruments that support small business eligibility including specific agreement types; list and summarize investor protection agreements; list separately and in the aggregate gross revenues for applicant and related entities; include documentation for rural telephone cooperative exemptions if seeking that exemption; list and summarize agreements for use of spectrum capacity; and if claiming rural service provider bidding credit, provide required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements and instruments include articles of incorporation, by-laws, partnership agreements, shareholder agreements, voting/trust/management/franchise agreements, spectrum leasing/resale arrangements, letters of intent, and oral or written agreements. Summaries should reference specific provisions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction prior to grant: when permitted and prohibition on operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for licenses awarded by competitive bidding may construct facilities to provide service prior to grant of their applications, but must not operate such facilities until the FCC grants an authorization. An applicant may begin construction upon release of the Public Notice listing the post-auction long-form application for that facility as acceptable for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the FCC notifies the applicant that construction should not start or should stop while application is pending, the applicant must not begin or must stop immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption of risk for pre-grant construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants that begin construction before receiving authorization do so at their own risk and have no recourse against the United States for losses resulting from: applications not granted; errors or delays in issuing public notices; having to alter, relocate or dismantle the facility; or incurring costs necessary to bring the facility into compliance with applicable laws or FCC rules and orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for pre-grant construction
rubrics_metrics.description: All pre-grant construction is subject to conditions: (1) the application does not include a request for a waiver of one or more FCC rules; (2) for construction exceeding § 17.7, the licensee has notified FAA (Form 7460-1) and filed FCC Form 854; (3) the applicant has indicated in the application that the proposed facility would not have a significant environmental effect as per §§ 1.1301–1.1319; (4) individual international coordination with a foreign administration is not required under applicable international agreements and rules; and (5) any service-specific restrictions not listed herein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reportable eligibility events requiring Commission approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated entity must seek Commission approval for all reportable eligibility events. A reportable eligibility event includes: (1) any spectrum lease or other type of spectrum use agreement with one entity or cumulatively that might cause a licensee to lose eligibility for installment payments, a set-aside license, or a bidding credit (or a particular level of bidding credit) under § 1.2110 and applicable service-specific rules; and (2) any other event that would lead to a change in the eligibility of a licensee for designated entity benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and filing obligations for reporting eligibility events
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated entity filing an application reporting an eligibility event must list and summarize on the application all agreements and arrangements giving rise to or relating to the event, including parties (and affiliates, controlling interests, affiliates of controlling interests, spectrum lessees, resellers and wholesalers) and dates; file a copy of each agreement; and maintain at its facilities or with its designated agents for the term of the license the lists, summaries, dates, and copies of agreements and arrangements required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fees for eligibility event filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The application reporting the eligibility event will be treated as a transfer of control for purposes of determining the applicable application fees as set forth in § 1.1102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined processing timelines for eligibility-event applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility event applications will be placed on public notice once sufficiently complete and accepted for filing. Petitions to deny must comply with § 1.939 and be filed no later than 14 days following the Public Notice listing the application as accepted for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No later than 21 days following the Public Notice, the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau will grant, deny, or remove the application from streamlined processing for further review. Grants are reflected in a Public Notice promptly. If removed from streamlined processing, the Bureau will issue Public Notice and will either act within 90 days or provide notice that an additional 90-day review period is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice placement for eligibility-event applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications under this section will be placed on an informational public notice on a weekly basis (see § 1.933(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of eligibility-event application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must contain all information requested on the applicable form, any additional information and certifications required by the rules in this chapter, and any rules pertaining to the specific service for which the application is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing update duty for designated entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The designated entity is required to update any change in a relationship that gave rise to a reportable eligibility event.
